source.title: A Single Suffix to Break Them All: Basin-Aware Jailbreaks for Merged Model Families
source.authors: Yu Zhe; Yixin Tan; Junhao Wei; Wang Chen

page_placements.theme: Model, adapter and cache composition can transmit or repair safety loss

record.file_problem: None noted; the provided text appears to contain the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether adversarial suffixes raise harmful-response rates, including transfer across merged model families, and reports a separate evaluation of benign instruction fine-tuning. These are conceptual tests of V4 and V2, not reproductions of the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper's BAJ attack appends adversarial suffixes to harmful requests and measures harmful-response success, so its attack results bear on V4. Appendix B evaluates safety after benign task fine-tuning, bearing on V2. The paper does not measure per-token KL, compliant prefilled openings, localized safety parameters, or safety-depth training. Claims and results cited from prior work are not extracted as findings. The probe-direction and attack-optimization details are methods, not separate results on those untested versions.
record.test_reason: The paper's own results bear on V4: a suffix attack on merged models derived from safety-aligned backbones is measured. It also bears weakly on V2: benign task fine-tuning is evaluated for harmful compliance. Both are new settings, not reproductions of the original methods, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct: the authors conclude that merged models from the same pretrained backbone share jailbreak vulnerabilities even when constituents are individually aligned, and that BAJ suffixes transfer across merging methods, deployments and defenses. One correction: the authors also report that an adaptive fine-tune on BAJ refusal pairs substantially reduces TSR (Appendix K), and that BAJ is much less effective on unmerged fine-tuned models.
record.recipe_differences: This paper studies a mutation-based adversarial-suffix attack on merged model families and benign task fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the original harmful-data fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack transfer differs between merged models and standard fine-tuned models without merging. The paper also reports changes under defenses, but the defense table generally leaves substantial attack success; perplexity filtering leaves its reported TSR unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Suffixes optimized on one pretrained backbone's merged family transfer poorly to other backbones (Figure 1, off-diagonal), and merged models stay safe without attack (Table 6, ASR 0-0.04).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Merging-based safety erosion: jailbreak transfer depends on a shared pretrained backbone, not on constituent models.

record.problems: The paper reports no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its principal TSR/ASR results. The benign-fine-tuning outcomes are described as near-zero in the text and shown in a figure rather than fully enumerated as text values. BAJ outputs were human-checked on a sample of 50 successful attacks, but the main rate tables rely on an LLM judge.
record.rows_left_out: To remain within the 60-row limit, omitted Table 2's 24 BAJ results across merging methods and deployment configurations; Table 1's no-attack and comparator-attack rows; Appendix B Table 6's merged-model no-attack ASRs; Appendix E ablations and Appendix F matched-surrogate baselines; and Appendix K adaptive-defense results. These sections report additional BAJ/safety-related results, but the retained rows cover the tested versions and prioritize per-model/task outcomes and defense conditions.

untested.parts: No comparison of ordinary versus carefully selected benign data; no few-example regime; no fine-tuned-versus-pretrained numbers beyond the figure.
No prefilling or decoding changes; only suffixes.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
No test of data or objective causes.

missing.what: No-attack baseline (0.0) and comparator-attack TSRs (GCG, AutoDAN, etc.) for the same merged families
Adaptive-defense TSR after fine-tuning on BAJ refusal pairs (18.4, 15.6, 20.7)
Merged-model no-attack ASRs (0.0-0.04), a baseline for judging safety after merging

record.verdict_notes: Weak for V2: ASR is on plain AdvBench with no attack, the figure is not tabulated, and the fine-tuning recipe differs from the original source. The paper frames benign fine-tuning as a control, not a test of V2. V4 evidence is about adversarial suffixes optimized on merged surrogates, not prefilling. The judge is an LLM classifier (HarmBench, Llama-2-13B), with a 50-sample human check. No uncertainty is reported. The probe-direction objective is a method detail.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not fine-tune on harmful examples to test whether that removes refusal.
It evaluates benign task fine-tuning, but does not compare ordinary versus carefully selected benign datasets or test the original claim's few-to-hundreds-example scale.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models is reported.
It tests adversarial suffixes, but not compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization test is reported.
It does not test whether the data or objective of safety training produces shallow safety.
It does not train safety to extend beyond initial response tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.
